utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. Case Number IT-02-60-T, The Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. I'm very sorry for the delay. Maybe that's because of the Monday phenomenon. Before we have the next witness, are there any matters the parties would like to bring to the attention of this Bench? Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We, as I think Your Honour knows, we are out of order from our original order due to a serious illness of one of the witnesses. But we do have a witness ready to go, and this happened the last minute this last weekend, but we have put everyone on notice of that change.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, good morning. I just want to say that I really believe that it violates Mr. Jokic's rights to be prepared for the witnesses. Though I do understand that illnesses happen, but we got a call at 5.00 yesterday evening announcing the change in the witness schedule. And when you work all weekend to prepare for a witness and then all of a sudden at 5.00 the day before, I think it surprises the Defence, takes us by surprise and doesn't give us enough time to prepare for the witness. We will go forward today because Mr. Stojanovic had already prepared for the second witness, but we think as a rule, it should not become a common practice and if there's another delay like this we should be granted a 24-hour period to prepare. But we will go forward today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And I believe that during the proceedings, there might be something extraordinary happens here and there, and I hope that both parties could understand the difficulties facing by the other party during the proceedings in calling the witnesses. I think this rule applied to both parties. And in the future, in the Defence case, and there should be at least 24 hours previous notice for changing of the witnesses. But we are lucky that the testimony of this witness or the first two witnesses are not very long. I believe that if the first witness will appear, we'll hear the two witnesses today. So I believe Defence party has prepared for the cross-examination of that witness. Having said that, could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper the usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. McCloskey:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us your name, please.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: My name is Mevludin Oric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you spell your last name?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: O-R-I-C.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you Muslim by faith?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you born?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: In Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you living in 1995?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I lived in the village of Lehovici in Srebrenica Municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do there?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I lived with my family, with my wife and children. And I defended my home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a member of the Bosnian/Muslim army in the enclave?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I was a member of the reserve force. I did not have a rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on July 11th, what did you decide to do? What did you and your family decide to do?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: On the 11th of July, I was mobilised. I was told to go to the line to defend the defence line, and then Srebrenica fell in the evening, at about 6.00. My family went to Potocari to the UNPROFOR base, and I stayed in the village of Susnjari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what defence line area were you in? Near what villages?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Near the village of Brezova Njiva and Jaglici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what time did you get to Susnjari on the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I arrived in the evening, at about 6.00 or 7.00, and we were told to gather there and to see what we would do next and where we would set off to, either towards Tuzla or towards Zepa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the final decision about Tuzla or Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: The order of the main commander, the one who was the commander of Srebrenica, told us that we should go in the direction of Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us your best estimate of how many able-bodied men were gathering around Susnjari that night of the 11th?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Between that night and in the morning before dawn broke, that was about 15.000 men. There were also children there and men over 65 years of age, and children up to 15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at what time and what day did you actually start off with this group towards Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: One group set off in the evening while I left on the 12th of July at about 9.00 or 10.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 12 July, 9.00 or 10.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: That's right, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know what part of this big column you were in?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I was by the end of the column. Most of the people went ahead of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your hike towards Tuzla on the 12th and the afternoon, evening of the 12th, was the part of the column where you were attacked?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Just as we set off, we were shelled by anti-aircraft weapons, fired on. And throughout the time that we travelled, we were ambushed, we were shelled by mortars, we were fired on by snipers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you decide to spend the night of the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Near the village of Kamenica, and this is where the largest ambush was. That's where my father went missing, and my relatives. That was the largest ambush that I went through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen your father since that day, 12 July?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the morning of the 13th of July, can you describe where you were and what you did.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: On the 13th of July, in the morning, I was there, the ambush, and we were told that we should set off and go further. We couldn't stay the night there. They were infiltrating their own people in the group, and we were going around into the fields. And we -- I set off towards Konjevic Polje. That night, when the light started, when the day broke, that was near the village of Sandici. Again, there was ambush there because one of the Serb soldiers took us. He was in our civilian clothes, and he took us towards that ambush. And I managed to get away from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I returned to a wood, that's where I spent the night. The next day, when it was light, I didn't know what time it was, I didn't have a watch, I found a group of 13 people, and we set off over some hills towards Konjevic Polje because there was a young man who came from Konjevic Polje, and he knew the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this on the 13th of July you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: That's right, yes, the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell us what happened as you came closer to Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We arrived at a hill above Konjevic Polje, that's where we spent the entire day. There were groups coming and going. They were going into reconnaissance. Nobody was returning. I stayed with my group the whole time. We were also shelled there by mortars, also they used Praga weapon. That's where I spent all the time until dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you -- did you finally surrender or were you captured?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I waited for the dark so that I would try and cross the road going towards Cerska, and I set off with my group. We were not armed. We didn't even have any weapons. And we set off towards the road. There were trees around there. There were a lot of bramble bushes. And when we got to the road, behind us we heard the clicking of the rifles and we were told not to escape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So then what happened?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We had no choice. If we were going to run towards Konjevic Polje, they were along the road all the way from Kasaba to Kravica, that they held the road, everything was blocked. So we didn't have anywhere to go, so we surrendered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many Serb personnel did you surrender to?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how many people were in those bramble bushes. Maybe four or five. One man approached me who knew me. He's from Potocari. His last name is Gligic. I've forgotten his first name. He approached me, and he asked "do you know me?" And I said I did. And then they searched me, myself and others. And we were told to put our hands on our head and we should run on the road to Konjevic Polje to the centre. We were then taken to a warehouse. That warehouse was an agricultural retail store warehouse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us, do you know about what year Mr. Gligic was born in?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure. I think he was born in 1968 or 1969 because he went to school in Potocari where I went as well. So I do know him quite well. And my sister also went to school with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What village was he originally from?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: The village of Studenac, near Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now this warehouse where you were taken at the Konjevic Polje intersection, can you tell us what is there today in that location?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: That location is a gas station because that warehouse was destroyed and a gas station was built.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how many Muslim prisoners were at this warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: My group, nine of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened at the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: When they brought us to the warehouse, there was an officer who came. His shirt was undone. And he said: "Where are your rifles?" And he swore. And we said that we didn't have any rifles, that we had none, and that officer, in my opinion, that officer was from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what do you base your opinion on that this officer was from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: According to his speech and his uniform, to his ways of discipline, because I had served in the JNA, Yugoslav People's Army, and he didn't mistreat us. The way he acted towards us, he asked us if we were hungry, if we were thirsty. He brought us some water. He didn't bring it personally, but a soldier did that he had ordered to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers that appeared to be dressed similar to him?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw soldiers who were dressed similar to him, and they also had camouflage flak jackets on. They were from the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, what do you base your opinion that these were soldiers from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: The flak jackets, the uniform, and the discipline.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone bring you any food while you were in that warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: This officer said to us that we would have food brought to us, but when he returned later, he said that the dogs had eaten everything and there was no food left. They brought us a beer. They gave us cigarettes. But there was no food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone tell you where you were going to be going?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: He said to me that his orders were just to arrest us there, to take us prisoner, and to send us to Bratunac. The soldier who guarded us said that he didn't know what would happen to us. There was a small window there, and he said if you can escape through that window, do escape, but the window was small and we didn't manage to get out through it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Well, they told us to wait for buses. I think these buses were driving women and children from Potocari. Three buses returned. They took us out. It was already dark. The lights were on on the buses, not all of them, though. We boarded the first bus. They put us in the back seats. Three policemen boarded the bus, three military policemen from Republika Srpska. They were wearing blue UNPROFOR flak jackets from Srebrenica. And then we set off towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, how do you know that these were military policemen?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: That is what was written on their arms. It said "Military police of Republika Srpska." They had white belts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what I'd also -- if you could, take a look hopefully on your screen, you'll see a picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And for the record, this is Exhibit P22, chapter 16, page 6, for the record.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see that photograph?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does anything in that photograph look familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: This flak jacket is very familiar to me, both from Srebrenica and from those policemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that the flak jacket, the blue flak jacket with the number 2 on it in the photo?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In a previous statement, did you tell an interviewer that there were police officers in blue uniforms that got on the bus?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: No, I said they had flak jackets on, blue UNPROFOR flak jackets from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And once you got on the buses and these military police officers got on the buses, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We went towards Bratunac. We stopped in Kravica on the right-hand side by the warehouse in Kravica. There was a large group of people who were sitting on a meadow between the road and the warehouse. That's where they stopped, and once all three buses were full, we set off towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did your buses take on people from this meadow?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How dark was it at this time that you're at Kravica?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: It was dusk, lights were just being turned on. But it could be seen that this meadow right by the road was full of people, and that they were surrounded by the military. I could see that very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get a look over at the big agricultural warehouse there?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was behind their backs. They were sitting in front of this warehouse and facing the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any Muslims in the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any bodies around the area anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did your bus go after Kravica?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We went to Bratunac in front of the Vuk Karadzic school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How well did you know these streets and the locations of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I know them well because I was born there. I lived there. I spent more time in Bratunac than in Srebrenica before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I want to show you an exhibit, P65, if we could put it on the ELMO. When you met with ICTY investigators, it's years ago now, did you write out a sketch for them of Bratunac and where your bus was by the school?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in looking at this Exhibit 65 on the ELMO, is this the copy of the drawing that you did for the ICTY investigators?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I see that in that drawing, you've noted Skola VK. Is that the school of Vuk Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you point with the little pointer there where you have drawn buses on this diagram.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: These are the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And could you take a marker. There should be a black marker, pen, in front of you. And if you could -- do you remember -- I see that there looks like four little rectangles there. Are those four buses you've drawn in?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember which one of the buses you were in?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I didn't have enough room on this sketch to draw yet another bus in, too. I was in the third bus. There were two buses behind me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Why don't you just circle the bus that you think you were in just from your diagram.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And then we have another exhibit I want to show you. Did you have a chance yesterday in my office to take a look at an aerial image of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's a little harder to make out on the ELMO. But were you able to in my office circle the Vuk Karadzic -- identify and circle the Vuk Karadzic school?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is this exhibit, which is P66, is this the picture that -- where you circled the school and put your initials?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. So could you tell if there was anybody -- could you see the school from your bus?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I could see the school. I saw the school. I could see the windows. Yes, I could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if there was any Muslim men in that school that night that you were there?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: They were taking men from the buses to the school, but they weren't bringing them back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why don't you describe for us what happened that night. Just tell us where you were and where you spent the night and what happened.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I spent that night in my seat, all night. They told us that there wasn't enough room in the school, that we had to stay on the buses. Soldiers came. They walked around the buses. They entered the buses. They asked questions. They asked if there was anybody from Susnjari, Osat, Osmace, Jadar, and that they should say so. Nobody said a thing. Then a man who I knew from before the war, Ilija, he took people from the bus to the school -- from the bus to the school, and then they called out a name, Catic or Djanic. I can't remember. They took him and they didn't return him to my bus. In the first seat, there was a man who was a bit mentally deranged and he fell asleep in that seat and we were told we were not allowed to sleep. And then this policeman wearing the blue flak jacket walked up to him and woke him up abruptly. And then he accidentally hit him on the flak jacket just like that as he was awakened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this a policeman or a military policeman?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: It was a military policeman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry for interrupting. And you were describing how the -- what happened again? Could you just tell us that again.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: He hit him on the flak jacket, I mean the prisoner did. And he turned to the other policeman and said: "Look at him, he hit me." And he cursed. And then the buses -- and then the soldiers that were in front of the bus said "Let's kill him, let's slaughter him, throw him out." And then he was taken out and they took him towards the school. And then I heard a short burst of gunfire. I could not see the face of the man who killed him there by the bus. I saw his back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the military police officer whose flak jacket he hit involved in any of this?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: He's the one who pushed him out to the soldiers who were outside, and also these two policemen who were with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the two policemen that were with him, were those policemen -- civilian policemen or military policemen?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: They were military policemen who were escorting us, who were actually providing security for the bus that had taken us there from Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So from your bus that night, how many men were taken out and didn't come back?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Two men were taken out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those were the two men you've just described for us.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes. One man, they beat, but they did not take him out of the bus. They asked who had ambushed some Serb soldiers up there. They got killed in this ambush. And he asked him who it was that ambushed them. And he beat him on the head, stomach, thighs, but they didn't take him out because a military policeman walked up to this soldier and kicked him out of the bus because he had been drunk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So are you saying a soldier came on to the bus and beat up one of the prisoners but then was kicked out by a military police officer?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what do you know about other Muslims from the other vehicles? Do you know if anything happened to any of them that night?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: All night they were taking groups out of the bus and taking them to school. All night, shooting could be heard from the school. People were screaming, moaning. It was horrible to listen to that kind of thing all night. But we had to. Whoever was taken out in those groups was never returned to the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone come and explain to you what the gunfire was about?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Well, they told us that they were sending off some young conscripts, sending them off to the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you believe that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened the next morning?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: The next morning, this was the 14th, the morning of the 14th, they told us that they were taking us to Kladanj to be exchanged as prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you see?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We waited there for a while, for this column to start. We were told that we had to wait. When we left Bratunac, we parked at the Vihor parking lot. We waited there, and we were told that we had to wait for UNPROFOR because they were due to arrive from Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you left the area in front of the Vuk Karadzic school, did you see any Muslim men come out of that school?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And about how many vehicles were over by the Vihor garage while you were waiting there?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: While we were waiting there, people asked the guards whether they could go there because it was possible to go to the toilet because people couldn't go to the toilet all night. They allowed us to do so. I didn't go out, though, but the men sitting next to me did go out. And they saw behind us, there had been a total of five buses and four trucks in that column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you been given any food that night in the bus parked in front of the Vuk Karadzic school?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: They didn't give us food, only water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the way -- well, at the Vihor garage, did they give you any food for the trip to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: They didn't give us any food. Only a woman, an elderly woman walked into the bus. She swore at us. She swore at our balija Turk mothers, and that -- she said that her son was killed and she would kill all of us, but then they got her off the bus, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "they got her off the bus," who was that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: At that moment, it was still the military police. After that, I don't know how much time had gone by, then a small military TAM truck came, and they took over from the police, and then three soldiers of the army of Republika Srpska took over instead of those three policemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: An APC came by, a white APC, with "UN" written on it. People who were sitting on the APC had UNPROFOR rifles and helmets. But I don't think they were UNPROFOR men because they were raising three fingers and greeting the soldiers who were guarding us on the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So was that the three-fingered Serbian salute that you saw them do?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the salute of Republika Srpska and Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So when this white APC came, what happened?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We set out towards Konjevic Polje, but they told us that we were going to Kladanj to be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you got to Konjevic Polje, did you turn left towards Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: No, we turned right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe to us where you went.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We turned right. When we came underneath the rocks, I mean, that place is called -- well, it's below Udrc. There are these big rocks there. They told us to put our heads down between our legs and not to watch where we were going. That's the road towards Drinjaca, between Konjevic Polje and Drinjaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After doing that, were you able to make out where you were going?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I was sitting in the back seat, and this seat is a bit higher than the rest. And even as I put my head down, I could see between my fingers where we were going. I could see through the window.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Trial Chamber where you saw the bus go.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We were going through Drinjaca. We came to Zvornik. We passed the town because I know the town of Zvornik. We went by the bus station, and the department store, and we went on to Karakaj. There's a factory there, a bauxite factory. We went by it. And then we turned left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, turning left by Karakaj, what direction -- what town is in that direction?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: That road leads to Tuzla, but we didn't ride along that road for a long time. We turned right again. I was looking through my fingers, but I didn't know the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after you turned right off the main road towards Tuzla, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We came to a school. We were in front of this school. That's where they told us to lift our hands and that we were allowed to look around again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what did you see there at this school? Can you describe what you saw when you were able to look around clearly.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We got there to the school. I saw a big sports field with nets, protective nets, so that the ball wouldn't get off the field. I saw a monument made of stone. I don't know whose monument it is, though. I saw this school with a gym. I saw the buses. The APC that was escorting us stood behind the buses, and an anti-aircraft gun was pointed at us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any Serb personnel around these buses at the school?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: On both sides, on the right-hand side and on the left-hand side, all the way up to the entrance into the school so that no one would try to run away. They had rifles, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say there was a playing field by the school. Was that a hardtop playing field or a grass or dirt playing field?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Hardtop, concrete.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what happened when you got off your bus?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We were running along to the entrance to the school on the right-hand side. I saw that everybody had to throw aside whatever they were holding in their hands before entering the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any collection of stuff there?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Before the entrance on the right-hand side, before the entrance to the corridor, I saw berets, jackets, coats. Anything that you had in your hands you had to throw aside. You were not allowed to take it inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you got inside the school, what part of the school did you go to?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: To the right was the entrance to the school, and to the left was the way to the sports hall, to the gym. That's where we went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went into the gym, did you see any people there that weren't from your group?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: In the right-hand corner, there was a large group of people. They were sitting down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were these Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, because I knew some of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe how many people came into that gym and how that happened.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: About 2 and a half thousand people, according to my estimate, were pressed together in that gym.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "pressed together," how were you organised?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: My knees were below my chin. They forced us to. We had to. They said they would shoot if we didn't all press together, so people were fainting. A person would faint and couldn't fall, not to the left, not to the right. They would just continue sitting up unconscious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How hot was it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: It was too hot. And people had no water, so that's why they were fainting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of the fainted people or the injured people cared for by the troops that were guarding you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: To start with, we were not helped in any way. Perhaps later on, they asked if there was anyone below 18 years of age to come out of there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did some young -- some kids actually get pulled out from the crowd?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, two young boys who were perhaps 14 or 15 years of age. They went out. They went out into the corridor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the crowd given any water?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: They gave some canisters to these kids, and they took it round the hall to give to people to drink.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what happened in that gym that was jammed full of people like this?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: The first thing they did was to divide us in approximately four rows that would be sitting away from the wall and four rows to the left, four to the right, four facing the entrance. So all rows were distributed in this way. That's what they ordered us to do. That's how they ordered us to turn. I was facing the entrance door that I had come in through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anybody in that gym abused that day besides the general conditions?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: One of the prisoners, probably he felt ill. He got up, and we were told strictly not to get up. And he got up and he said: "What are you afraid of? There are plenty of us. Do not be afraid." Soldiers charged in. They said: "Who said that?" And he said he did. And they told him to get out. He didn't want to get out, and they said they would shoot. They would fire, kill 20, 30 people if he didn't get out. And then he was pushed out by the others so that they wouldn't be killed, those sitting next to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see what happened to this person that got pushed out?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes. There, right inside the corridor, just outside of the gym, I heard a short burst of fire. He screamed, and he was killed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any officers come by the gym that day?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mladic came with his entourage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did he stay?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: He didn't stay long. He spoke to the main person who was guarding us. He looked at us, laughed a bit, because when he was there and then he left, we were then -- afterwards we were immediately told we would be going to the Batkovic camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the process by which you and other Muslim prisoners were taken out of the gym that day.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Inside the gym, to my right-hand side, there was a smaller room. I think it was a kind of locker room or something like that. And that room had another door leading outside. That's where they brought tables. They brought some kind of wooden bars, placed it on the door. And they said we would be leaving one by one, that we shouldn't be pushing and that we shouldn't leave in a disorderly fashion. And that's how the leaving started.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did they do with people as they were exiting the gym?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: The first thing that was done, two of the prisoners were taken out, Nezir Gusic. I knew him because he was a neighbour, and they also brought out another one, Nezir tied the blindfold, and the other one was given water. Everybody had to drink some water. So they would take out 20, 30 people. Then they would put the bar down, and then the lorries would come. And that's how it went. I was in the sixth group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the soldiers that were around you when you got your blindfold and your water.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: There was a woman who was armed. She was in camouflage uniform, and there were three soldiers standing around with the rifles in that room where we were being blindfolded and given water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after you were blindfolded and given some water, were you put on a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We were loaded on to small TAM trucks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know what kind of truck it was if you were blindfolded?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Because very quickly, I took my blindfold off, and I also know the sound of the engine of that TAM truck and its size.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the back of the TAM truck, how it looked, what was there.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: It was covered with a tarpaulin cover, and it had two benches on either side. And in the middle, there was a larger tyre of a larger truck, a FAP truck, a FAP truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were put in the back of that truck, where did that truck go?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I felt that it had gone over some rail tracks, and we got to some kind of a meadow. That's where we stopped, and we were told to line up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for us what happened after that.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We got off the lorry, and we were told to line up as quickly as possible. When we did so, I was together with my cousin Hariz, and we held hands. And he said they would kill us. And I said they wouldn't. He didn't even finish speaking when the bursts of fire started.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what happened with the burst of fire.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: The burst of fire killed my cousin. He was shouting, screaming. I fell on the ground. He fell on top of me. That's when screaming and groaning of injured men started.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you hurt?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Afterwards, they continued to bring more shifts, more groups. They continued to execute those injured people who were screaming. They would be killed off. That's how it proceeded all the way until some people tried to escape. And one was killed, and one managed to escape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know roughly what time of day it was that your group was executed?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I think it was about 1.00 or 2.00. I didn't have a watch, so I can't say accurately what the time was. But I think it was about that time because the sun was high up, well high up. I think it was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the executions continue after dark?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know roughly how long after dark the executions continued?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I had fainted. And when I came round, I took the blindfold off slowly, off my eyes, and I saw some lights, headlights, of vehicles. Because there was a loader and an excavator. They were digging a grave. And there were headlights. They had brought another five groups after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any other lights in that field besides the lights of the heavy equipment you saw?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: No, none.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So could you tell how they were lighting up the executions that went on in the night, which piece of equipment they were using, or both?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: The engines were off, and I think it was from the ULT loaders that they were using the headlights. But the engines were not on, the machines were not working. The engines had been switched off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "ULT," is that a brand of a Yugoslav heavy equipment company?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Loader, a ULT loader, that's what we called it, loader, because it's used for -- it's used by building -- by building companies, construction companies. It can load, it can push soil in front of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And when you spoke to the ICTY investigators a long while back, the same time you drew that diagram of Bratunac, can you draw little diagrams of the two machines that you saw there that night, that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I'd like to object at this time because this witness has not been certified as to have any knowledge about this equipment one way or the other. So whether he knew about what an excavator was or what a ULT was, I think the Prosecutor needs to ask him a few more questions to clarify his expertise in this area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we are not such technicians. We do not know the difference between a loader or excavator or anything else. But anyway, the witness drew a picture of it. Let's look at the picture and see what it is. Yes, you may proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you draw a picture of those machines for the ICTY investigators a few years back?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I drew the picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this exhibit, P67, do you see that picture on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that a copy of the picture you drew for the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Starting with the machine on your left, could you describe what that is and just tell us a little bit about it and how you know about a machine like that.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: On my left-hand side is the excavator which is used for digging. It has a scoop which can dig deep into the soil.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what kind of wheels or tracks did you see on that excavator?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: The excavator doesn't have wheels. It has caterpillar tracks. This one doesn't have wheels, the one on the drawing. There are also excavators that have wheels, but the one that was digging the grave has tracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And so let's go to the other piece of equipment. Now, what is that and what does it do?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: And the drawing on the right-hand side is a loader. It is used for loading soil on to the lorries. It can also push soil in front of it, and it is a vehicle on wheels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What colour was the loader that night, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: The loader was yellow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What colour was the excavator that night, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yellow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any time that night were you able to get a look at how many bodies were in that field around you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: It was a meadow full. I didn't count the bodies, but it was -- a meadow was full.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you -- and I don't want to ask you to spend the time to describe this, so if I could just ask you simply, were you able to crawl away from that horrible place and eventually escape to the free territory?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I couldn't crawl away. When I got up, I found Hurem who was alive. And I stepped across dead bodies, and there was too much blood that was beginning to congeal. So it was very hard. It was very slippery to walk there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you and Hurem were eventually able to escape to the free territory?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. President, Your Honours, I don't have any other questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll have a break now. We'll resume at 10 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any cross-examination? Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I just have a few questions. Cross-examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. As I understand it, back on August 12th, 1995, you gave a statement.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I have before me a statement that seems to have been signed by you, and it's dated 12 August, 1995, where you describe the events, and I believe it might have been at that time when you made the drawings that we saw today.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before coming here today, did you have an opportunity to review that statement with the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would it -- was that as late as yesterday that you reviewed your statement?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in your statement, it indicates that you were at the time of the fall of Srebrenica a commander of a 10-member infantry unit of the 283rd Brigade of the 2nd Corps of the BiH army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from reading your statement, it also appears that when everybody gathered on the 11th or the 12th to leave Srebrenica, there were also men from the 284th Brigade along with the 283rd Brigade of the 2nd Corps of the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Everyone was together in Susnjari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, today you indicated that there were approximately 1500 -- 15.000 men that had gathered to form the column. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes. Among them were also children and elderly people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And in your statement you also indicated that before the fall of Srebrenica, there were about 14.000 BiH soldiers in the Srebrenica region.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Not all of them were soldiers, and there were also people who had gone to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me repeat my question again. In your statement, you state: "Before the fall of Srebrenica, there were about 14.000 BiH soldiers in the Srebrenica region." Do you recall reading that in your statement yesterday before coming here today?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: There were. There were 14.000 people, but not all of them had rifles, not all of them were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me -- before I show you your statement, I'm going to read it one more time, and I want you to see if you would agree with me. In your statement, you say: "Before the fall of Srebrenica, there were about 14.000 BiH soldiers in the Srebrenica region." That's what you state. Now, do you recall reading that or would you like to look at your statement to refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I have stated that. Yes, I had read the statement. I read the statement yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what's in your statement that you wrote or you gave on August 12th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, just one more area: You indicate at times in your statement that there were JNA soldiers, and you distinguished them from the Chetniks, which you considered the Bosnian Serb soldiers. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to you, a Chetnik was somebody, at least in your statement, was a soldier who was not clean-cut, did not look very disciplined, did not behave in a disciplined manner?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Versus the JNA soldiers, they looked more professionally dressed, and they were more disciplined?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But -- and then you did indicate that you were able to recognise some distinction in the dialect that they spoke, so that was another characteristic that you were -- you factored in into your opinion as to whether they were Chetniks or whether they were JNA?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I think they were members of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic, your cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Witness. Cross-examined by Mr. Stojanovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Considering that we are speaking the same language, we have previous experience that it would be good if you could wait for the interpretation to finish before you answer. Thank you. Bearing in mind the interviews that you have given so far and the exhibits and the evidence given to us by the Prosecutor before your testimony today, I'd like to ask you just a few questions just to clarify and to make sure that this is correct. First of all, is it true that beginning of 1992, you were in Croatia where you worked when the war started?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that in January 1992, of your own will, that is, out of your own initiative, as you say here, you went to military training in Makarska, it's a town located in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I went to work there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in Makarska, were you there for military training for 27 days?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me who trained you there, who provided this military training?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I reported to the MUP in the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "MUP of the Croatian army," I just want to make sure whether I'm understanding you correctly. Is it MUP as a civilian structure or is it the military police with the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Civilian Croatian police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. After that military training, did you take part in the war events that took place in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: In Capilinja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it, then, true that together with the volunteers' regiment called King Tomislav [phoen] took part in the occupation of the JNA barracks in Capilinja?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us just confirm, is it true to say that that was in January 1992?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: No, no, it wasn't January.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us which month it was, then?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I don't recall which month it was. I think it was in spring when firing started in Mostar, we then went to Capilinja to defend the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it mean that that was in the spring of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true that all this was happening before the conflict, events broke out in Bosnia-Herzegovina and in the area of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I to conclude that this was April, May, or some other spring months in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, war was happening in Srebrenica in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you took the barracks in Capilinja?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that after, that you went to the front line in Orasje, the town located in northern Bosnia and which at the time was under the control of the then Croatian part of the Herceg Bosna army?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I set off towards Tuzla from Zagreb. We tried to get through Orasje, but we couldn't because it was blocked in Podgajevi and Vidorice. And in Bosanski Samac. We had to wait there to liberate -- to have the territory liberated via Gradacac to get through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true that then, together with your friend, Elvir Maric, you arrived in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us which month in 1992 that was?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: That was in July 1992. Mid-July 1992 when I arrived in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that soon afterwards, you were tasked by Naser Oric to go to Tuzla for some medicine?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I to conclude that afterwards, together with 47 volunteers, you returned to Srebrenica after crossing the Serb positions?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, 47 people were carrying medicine, intravenous equipment and so on going from Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today, you confirmed followed by a question of Mr. Karnavas, and I'd just like to clarify one point. Is it true that in July 1995, you were a commander of a sabotage squad?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: It wasn't a sabotage squad. It was just an ordinary squad of the 283rd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were the commander, the commanding officer?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that as the commanding officer, the leader of that military formation, in July 1994 you had been tasked to guard the UNPROFOR base between the villages of Jaglici and Susnjari?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: It wasn't our task to protect the UNPROFOR base. After the 11th of July when Srebrenica fell and UNPROFOR withdrew, we then took up that position so that they wouldn't get through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that you used multiple rocket launcher to prevent the UNPROFOR personnel from leaving that position?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I didn't have a Zolja. That is a multiple rocket launcher, or a rifle or grenades because that was taken away from me by UNPROFOR. I didn't have that, I only have a couple of hand grenades.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know there were warnings to UNPROFOR soldiers that if they withdrew from their position, this anti-tank weapon would be used against them?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I wasn't there when that was happening. I was there when women stood in front of the APC not wanting to let them withdraw. I wasn't present when this other thing was happening. I didn't even hear about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when they withdrew with your unit, you took up that position so that there wouldn't be a breakthrough through that position. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'm going to finish by asking, is it correct to conclude that the moment of your capture, because today at the Prosecutor's question, you said you were captured, you were at the time a member of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have another group of questions that we wanted to ask.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there is just something we would like to clarify regarding the transport from Bratunac to the school that you have described. You said that in the morning, the 13th of July, you were next to the garage of the Vihor company, and that you were there for a while waiting, as you were told, for UNPROFOR vehicles. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. That was 14th in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 14th, very well, thank you. That's my mistake. And these UNPROFOR vehicles, did they arrive?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: One UNPROFOR APC arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described it, and you said that it was leading, it was heading the column. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: When we set off, it was leading the column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that escorting, or rather servicing this APC, there were soldiers who were wearing helmets and flak jackets with UN insignia?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, and rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And rifles. Thank you. For the sake of the Trial Chamber, because we know the position -- we know the layout. But when you're going from the school where you were, do you have to go through the entire town of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I don't know which school you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The school in Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We passed through town by the bus station. We went by the department store. I know this town well. We went by the apartment buildings that are on the right-hand side, all the way to Karakaj, to Glinice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you were passing through Zvornik, did you stop anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We didn't stop anywhere until the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until the school. Thank you. Was it being mentioned then also that you were going for an exchange?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: They told us in Bratunac that we would be exchanged, that we were going for an exchange, and they didn't tell us anything before we were taken to the execution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today you confirmed that as you were getting off the buses near the gym, that you saw this vehicle with UNPROFOR insignia again. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, there is a road by the school, and it stopped -- it had parked by the road, and its PAM, its anti-aircraft gun was pointing at the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If I understood you correctly, you know Zvornik quite well, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can tell us, then, where the Standard factory is in Zvornik or in Karakaj?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But may I ask you, would it be right if I say that in Zvornik and Karakaj, you did not stop all the way up to the school when you got off the buses?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We didn't stop anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing more, thank you. And by your leave, just another group of questions which have to do with the position of the site that you were at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today you said, and this was also included in the statement that you gave to the Prosecution earlier on, you said that you had the impression that you had been driving in that small TAM truck on a road that was bumpy, that you continued your journey over two hills, and that the truck stopped soon after you crossed the rail tracks. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: No, we just crossed the rail tracks. We felt that. We felt that because the truck went up and down. But we didn't cross any hills, any hillocks, whatever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I conclude, then, that you're sure that you crossed a railroad or is this something that you inferred?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We did cross a railroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to ask at this point in time to have an exhibit returned. Anyway, it was marked ERN 00336998. The witness gave his explanations in this regard while giving a statement to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. That is the internal ICTY number. I think it would be best if we could get Defence exhibit numbers so we can distinguish what we're talking about here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it's a very good idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to thank the Prosecution and I wish to thank the honourable Trial Chamber. Now I have a question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the fact that he referred a short while ago that he crossed a railroad, could you just show on this sketch the actual place where he thinks they set out from as they went to the execution site?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: On the left-hand side of this picture, you can see a railroad. It's there. It's below this other place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I infer that in your opinion, on the 14th in the evening, both machines were on the other side of the railroad?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: The machines were underneath the hill that's drawn here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please use that pointer and indicate for the Trial Chamber and for me the position that you were in in relation to the machines.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I was here approximately, closer to the railroad. This is where the execution finished, and the machines remained there below the hill. And I went on this other side when I got up. I went this way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's confirm once again, does this mean that the machines were on the same side of the railroad as you were on the 14th in the evening?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since we will be using this when adducing evidence, could the witness please mark the place where he was approximately on that night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do have that magic marker.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I was approximately here, here. Because when I got up, I found Hurem here approximately, and then went further on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please use that pen or marker, whatever, to mark the place that you were at that evening, the 14th. You can also put a circle around it.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you use a dotted line to show where you went as you were running away.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: [Marks] These two dots depict the place where I found Hurem and the two wounded men who stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you just place the date there, the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: It was after 2.00 at night, so it was already the 15th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please put the 15th of July, 2.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: When I set out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, the 15th of July, but could you also please put 2.00 a.m. as well so that we know it happened at 2.00 so it's 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I just ask you to write that down, 2.00, please, because it's very important for us, 2.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether it was exactly 2.00. It was after midnight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you can put, say, between 12.00 and 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can you tell us approximately now how far away you were from these machines.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. They were near me, and I was afraid they would get really close to me and kill me. I was still alive, and I was blindfolded but it felt that way. That's the way I heard them, as if they were nearby.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From this distance, could you see who was operating these machines? Was this person in civilian or military clothing?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I was blindfolded. I was lying on the ground. I couldn't see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You couldn't see.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I couldn't see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said today that you saw two machines, one an excavator and the other one a loader.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you preclude the possibility of yet another excavator having been there, one that was not operated at the time as far as you could see?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I saw two that were behind the grave. They had parked there. They were not on. Two machines, that is to say, an excavator and a loader.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because Kemal Mehmedovic who was a witness who was also heard here and he said that the excavator had wheels. You said today that it had Caterpillars. Do you still abide by what you said, that the excavator had Caterpillar tracks?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I abide by my statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I infer on the basis of that that what Kemal Mehmedovic said is not correct with regard to the Caterpillars or rather the wheels?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's an improper question to ask him to conclude about the correctness of a specific evidence other witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so. Mr. Stojanovic, please withdraw this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just going to repeat this last question. Are you sure that the excavator had Caterpillars rather than wheels?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I have a few more questions to put to you in relation to your statement as well. You said today that you saw the lights of the loader that was lighting the excavation site.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: When I took off my blindfold, I saw the lights, and they could have come from the excavator.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I conclude on that basis that these were the headlights of one of the two machines that you saw, not both? Not both?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I think it was just one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You said further on in response to the Prosecution's questions that you heard the following words: "Do you have anyone to leave behind here to stand guard?" A discussion started as to who would stay behind. And then somebody said: "Why should we stay behind when they're dead?" Did you perhaps hear that any of the drivers of these machines said that they didn't want to stay there alone on their own?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you proceeded, somebody answered the soldiers that they could go, and that the lights on the excavator and on the bulldozer were turned off, and that you heard the vehicles leave. So is it correct for me to conclude on that basis that both vehicles then left?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: The TAM trucks that brought people left. The last time when they brought a group for the execution, and then this was heard. Somebody asked whether anybody should stay behind to stand guard, and then those vehicles left. However, the machines were off when I came to. When I say "the machines," I'm referring to the excavator and the loader, so they were off but only the lights were on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to finish by putting just a few more questions to you. Did you notice that people were buried on the 14th? As you lay there, were people buried?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I didn't notice any such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at the time of the execution, there weren't any burials?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: While I was awake, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I conclude on that basis that it is correct that this heavy machinery, the ULT, that is to say, the loader that you talked about today, was not providing light in the area where the victims were being buried into the mass graves at the moment when you were there, between the 14th and the 15th?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: No, during the day they were digging the mass grave. And at night, they were turned off when I came to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "turned off," you mean the machines were not operating at that moment?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: They weren't working.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were not active, and their lights were not on?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: They were not active. They were not working then. Only the lights were on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have just one more question for you. Can you recall whether there was any possibility that you crossed the railroad as you were fleeing from the site?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Not during that night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not during that night?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can I conclude that you were running in a direction that was opposite the railroad that you crossed while you were in the TAM truck?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We crossed the hill where there is a tunnel underneath, one that a railroad goes through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you were running away?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions. Thank you. And I thank the witness. I am sorry if there was anything personal regarding these questions. I try to be as objective and as impartial as possible in view of your position. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I was informed about the continuity of the document which is a sketch of a map used by the Defence team is D4/3.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just one question, if I may, Mr. President. Re-examined by Mr. McCloskey:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you left that field that night, that early morning of the 15th, were there any people that were still alive but yet unable to move?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
